draft.title: The Mandate of Heaven
card: The Mandate of Heaven was the idea that heaven gave a ruler the right to rule China. A dynasty is a line of rulers from one family.
The Mandate depended on good behaviour. A ruler was expected to govern fairly and look after the people.
Floods, famines and earthquakes, or large revolts, were seen as signs that heaven was unhappy. People took them as signs that a dynasty had lost the Mandate.
A new ruler who overthrew a dynasty could claim that heaven had passed the Mandate to him. This was used to explain why one dynasty replaced another.
draft.remember: Heaven gave the right to rule, and disasters or revolts were signs it could be lost.

a.q: What was the Mandate of Heaven?
opts: The idea that heaven gave a ruler the right to rule
A law that said the eldest son must become emperor
A promise that rulers would never face revolts
A rule that only priests could choose a new ruler
a.why: The Mandate was the belief that heaven gave a ruler the right to rule. It was not a guarantee, because a ruler who governed badly could lose it.
a.clue: Think about who was believed to give the right to rule.

b.q: In Ancient China, a river flooded and ruined crops across many provinces, and then farmers rose up against the emperor. How might people have explained these events?
opts: The dynasty had lost the Mandate of Heaven
The emperor had gained a stronger Mandate
The floods proved the dynasty was ruling fairly
The Mandate only applied to the emperor's family
b.why: Disasters and revolts were seen as signs that heaven had withdrawn its support, so people could say the dynasty had lost the Mandate. The idea that the floods showed fair rule is wrong, because the Mandate depended on good government and disasters were a warning sign.
b.clue: Disasters and revolts were read as signs from heaven.

a.best: The idea that heaven gave a ruler the right to rule

b.best: The dynasty had lost the Mandate of Heaven

a.q: Which statement best describes the Mandate of Heaven?
opts: Heaven's approval to rule, kept by governing well
Heaven's approval to rule, passed down to the eldest son
A written law that set out the duties of officials
The people's vote to choose who would be emperor
a.why: The Mandate was heaven's approval to rule, and it depended on the ruler governing fairly. It did not pass to the eldest son by birth: a dynasty could lose it, and a new ruler from another family could claim it.
a.clue: Could a ruler from a new family ever hold the Mandate?
